note: Quantity keys, units and physical bounds. quantity_rules.schema.json enforces exactly these; a test keeps the two identical. Extend only through a contract PR. Unit '1' means dimensionless.

flame_spread_rate.description: Rate of flame front advance over a solid fuel surface.

extinction_oxygen_mole_fraction.description: Lowest oxygen mole fraction at which a flame was sustained, as reported.

ignition_delay.description: Time from ignition energy onset to sustained flame, as defined by the source.

flame_length.description: Flame length as defined by the source.

flame_temperature.description: Flame or gas temperature as reported by the source.

initial_droplet_diameter.description: Droplet diameter at the source-defined time zero, as reported (FLEX: when the igniters are turned on). A droplet size, not a flame size.

visible_flame_extinction_diameter.description: Droplet diameter at the moment the visible flame extinguished, as reported by the source. A droplet size, not a flame size. A reported value may be a source estimate rather than a direct observation: NASA/TP-2015-216046 extrapolated the burning history when the droplet left the camera field of view before extinction, and Table IX does not mark which values were extrapolated. Present only when the source reports one; a reported value does not imply the test's recorded outcome (FLEX-001 is printed as Disruption with a reported value), and an absent value does not imply that extinction did not occur (FLEX-010 is printed as Extinction with a dash).

burning_rate_constant.description: Droplet burning-rate constant K, as reported by the source: the magnitude of the rate of decrease of droplet diameter squared with time, K = -d(D^2)/dt, so K is non-negative while the slope of D^2 versus t is negative. FLEX reports an average K from a linear fit of D^2 versus t from shortly after ignition to extinction. Not a flame spread rate; never interchangeable with flame_spread_rate.

burn_time.description: Duration of burning, as defined and reported by the source.
